patient_summary: Adult ED patient with equivocal right lower quadrant pain (no migration, no anorexia, afebrile, normal WBC; Alvarado 3) undergoing ultrasound for suspected appendicitis (synthetic).
pretest_source: Pickhardt 2011 p. 791 and Table 2 p. 792: 675/2871 = 23.5% of adults imaged by MDCT (applied here to an ultrasound-evaluated adult, a cross-modality assumption).

conditional_independence: Each case applies a single likelihood ratio (the LR for the result shown) to a single pretest probability, so no conditional-independence assumption is needed. If findings were ever combined, the LRs would be multiplied assuming conditional independence given disease status.

notes: The 23.5% prior comes from a CT-referred cohort and is applied to an ultrasound-evaluated patient (cross-modality assumption). Terasawa's ultrasound studies had pooled prevalence of about 50% (computed, Appendix Table 1). Alvarado score as written in the note (items in data/notes/facts/B6_appy_us.json): migration 0, anorexia 0, nausea 1, RLQ tenderness 2, rebound 0, T 37.1 0, WBC 9.4 0, left shift not reported 0; total 3. The presentation is deliberately equivocal so the 23.5% prior (all adults referred for CT) is a plausible pretest probability for the patient on the page. The Alvarado score is never stated in a note; facts identical to B5. Negative-result wording: the note says "no sonographic findings of appendicitis", the pooled-study definition of a negative scan. Terasawa 2004 (p. 541 and Appendix Table 1 footnote) defines a positive scan but not how a nonvisualized appendix was classified, so the pooled LR- 0.19 is applied to a generic negative ultrasound, not to a visualized, compressible normal appendix (which would justify a lower posttest probability than the 5.5% target).
